chunks: About the bathhouse, he said: “If he knows that he is a Christian, he should wash using other than the bathhouse water, unless he bathes alone at the basin, so he washes it and then bathes.” And he asked him about a Jew and a Christian putting his hand into water: may wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer) be performed from it? He said: “No, unless one is compelled to do so.”
(641) 24. As for the report that he narrated:
Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man: may he perform wudu (ablution) from the jug or vessel of another if he drank while being considered a Jew? He said: “Yes.” I said: From that very water from which he drinks? He said: “Yes.”

So this is to be understood as referring to when one drinks from it who is presumed to be a Jew, but that is not established with certainty; then it is necessary not to judge it impure except with certainty. Or it refers to one who had been a Jew and then accepted Islam. But as long as he is in the state of being a Jew, then wudu (ablution) with his leftover water is not permissible, according to what has preceded. Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: It is not permissible to purify oneself with the leftover water of a dog or a pig; and when a dog laps from a vessel, what is in it must be poured out, and it must be washed three times, twice with water and once with earth, with the earth being in the middle of the washings; then it is dried and used. This indicates that.

key_terms.اَلْحَمَّامِ: the bathhouse, in the context of shared bathing water
key_terms.بِالتُّرَابِ: with earth, used here as part of the vessel-cleansing procedure
key_terms.سُؤْرِهِ: leftover water or drink remaining after someone has used it
key_terms.وَلَغَ: lapped with the tongue, especially of a dog from a vessel

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed with water touched or drunk from by a Jew, Christian, dog, or pig?
ai.summary: This passage discusses rulings of ritual purity concerning water touched or used by Jews, Christians, dogs, and pigs. It includes a narrated report and then presents a juridical reconciliation limiting one report to uncertainty or prior conversion, while affirming that purification is not performed with certain impure leftovers.
